parameters.description:
Strategy to use to generate predictions.

* "most_frequent": the `predict` method always returns the most
  frequent class label in the observed `y` argument passed to `fit`.
  The `predict_proba` method returns the matching one-hot encoded
  vector.
* "prior": the `predict` method always returns the most frequent
  class label in the observed `y` argument passed to `fit` (like
  "most_frequent"). ``predict_proba`` always returns the empirical
  class distribution of `y` also known as the empirical class prior
  distribution.
* "stratified": the `predict_proba` method randomly samples one-hot
  vectors from a multinomial distribution parametrized by the empirical
  class prior probabilities.
  The `predict` method returns the class label which got probability
  one in the one-hot vector of `predict_proba`.
  Each sampled row of both methods is therefore independent and
  identically distributed.
* "uniform": generates predictions uniformly at random from the list
  of unique classes observed in `y`, i.e. each class has equal
  probability.
* "constant": always predicts a constant label that is provided by
  the user. This is useful for metrics that evaluate a non-majority
  class.

  .. versionchanged:: 0.24
     The default value of `strategy` has changed to "prior" in version
     0.24.
parameters.name: strategy

parameters.description:
Controls the randomness to generate the predictions when
``strategy='stratified'`` or ``strategy='uniform'``.
Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
parameters.name: random_state
parameters.type_doc: int, RandomState instance or None, default=None

parameters.description:
The explicit constant as predicted by the "constant" strategy. This
parameter is useful only for the "constant" strategy.
parameters.name: constant
parameters.type_doc: int or str or array-like of shape (n_outputs,), default=None
